issues.description: The total sample of 4,000 includes 1,500 individuals specifically recruited for having a past-year history of sports wagering. This oversampling of gamblers fundamentally distorts the sample composition and will inflate the base rate of gambling behavior relative to the general population. This creates an asymmetry across the behaviors being compared: gambling has an artificially enriched sample while other behaviors (especially prescription drug misuse and illicit drug use) do not. This could systematically bias comparisons of moral incongruence effects across behaviors, as the gambling analyses will have more power and a different distributional profile than other behaviors. The authors acknowledge this in their power analysis but do not adequately address how combining a representative sample with a targeted oversample affects the interpretability of cross-behavior comparisons.
issues.quote: Due to the design of the larger project from which this sample is taken, we will also recruit an additional 1,500 adults with recent (past year) history of wagering on sports generally or sporting events specifically.

issues.description: The authors acknowledge that for prescription drug misuse (estimated n=140) and illicit drug use (estimated n=240-480), the study is substantially underpowered to detect the small effects that are central to the hypotheses. For prescription drug misuse, estimated power is only .301, which means there is roughly a 70% chance of failing to detect a true effect at the SESOI. This means the equivalence tests for these substances are essentially uninformative, yet these behaviors are included as part of the hypothesis that moral incongruence does NOT predict substance use disorder symptoms. Failing to find an effect due to low power is not the same as demonstrating equivalence with null.
issues.quote: However, in the case of illicit drug use (prevalence estimated at 6%-12% of the population) and prescription drug misuse (prevalence estimated at 3.5% of the population), it is possible, if not probable, that our final sample sizes will fall below the minimum size required to detect effects that small (See Table 2).

issues.description: The study uses validated, behavior-specific measures for pornography (Brief Pornography Screen) and gambling (Problem Gambling Severity Index) but relies on modified NIDA-ASSIST items for all substance use outcomes. This creates a fundamental asymmetry in measurement quality and construct validity across the behaviors being compared. The modified NIDA-ASSIST items have not been validated for pornography or gambling use, and the substance use outcomes lack the psychometric rigor of the BPS and PGSI. Comparing interaction effects across behaviors measured with instruments of different validity and sensitivity is problematic, as differences in findings could be attributable to measurement differences rather than true differences in the moral incongruence effect.
issues.quote: Although such an approach is not currently validated for gambling or pornography, given the inclusion of other validated scales to assess these outcomes (see below), including them within the NIDA-ASSIST will not decrement our ability to evaluate our key hypotheses.

issues.description: The authors explicitly state they 'aim to demonstrate that—consistent with the ICD-11 decision—the role moral incongruence in predicting feelings of dysregulation is unique to sexual behavior.' This framing reveals a confirmatory orientation rather than a genuinely exploratory or balanced hypothesis-testing approach. For a registered report, this is concerning because it suggests the analytic decisions (e.g., the very conservative SESOI) may have been chosen to favor the desired outcome rather than to provide the most informative test.
issues.quote: Ultimately, we aim to demonstrate that—consistent with the ICD-11 decision to include moral distress as a diagnostic consideration when applying a diagnosis of CSBD—the role moral incongruence in predicting feelings of dysregulation is unique to sexual behavior, in contrast with other addictions.

issues.subcategory: SESOI justification and equivalence testing logic
issues.description: The SESOI of δ=.27 (standardized β=.11) is described as 'extremely conservative,' but the justification is circular. The authors chose the smallest observed effect from prior pornography studies as their SESOI, but this was from a study using religiousness (not moral disapproval directly) as the moderator and a different outcome measure. The authors then note that more parallel prior studies found much larger effects (β=.270). Using the smallest effect from a less-parallel study as the SESOI for equivalence testing of non-pornography behaviors creates an asymmetry that favors finding equivalence with null for those behaviors. Additionally, there is inconsistency: the text states SESOI of δ=.27 but then says it equals the β=.11 from prior work. The δ=.27 appears to come from a different study/effect entirely, creating confusion about what the actual equivalence bound is.
issues.quote: we elected to set our SESOI (δ) for our equivalence interval equal to the observed standardized estimate (β value) corresponding to the smallest effect listed above (β=.11, ΔR2 = .012, f2 = .016, Cohen's d = .25, Grubbs, Lee, et al., 2020).

issues.description: There is a clear inconsistency in the reported SESOI. The analytic plan states 'an equivalence region based on the smallest effect size of interest (SESOI) of δ= .27' but then later states the SESOI is set 'equal to the observed standardized estimate (β value) corresponding to the smallest effect listed above (β=.11).' These are different values (δ=.27 vs. β=.11), and it is unclear which is actually being used as the equivalence bound. This confusion undermines the interpretability of the planned equivalence tests.
issues.quote: We will use the Anderson-Hauck equivalence test for regression (Counsell & Cribbie, 2015), with an equivalence region based on the smallest effect size of interest (SESOI) of δ= .27.

issues.subcategory: Moral disapproval construct validity across domains
issues.description: The single-item measure of moral disapproval ('I believe that using ________ is morally wrong') may not capture the same construct across different behaviors. Moral disapproval of pornography is often rooted in religious/sexual values, while moral disapproval of illicit drugs may reflect legal/health concerns, and moral disapproval of gambling may reflect financial prudence concerns. The assumption that 'moral disapproval' functions equivalently across these domains is untested and potentially invalid. If the construct means different things across domains, then finding different interaction effects could reflect measurement non-equivalence rather than true differences in the moral incongruence phenomenon.
issues.quote: For each substance, we will ask participants to rate their agreement with the following statement 'I believe that using ________ is morally wrong' on a scale of 1 (strongly disagree) to 7 (strongly agree).

issues.description: The study is entirely cross-sectional, which limits causal inference. The interaction between moral disapproval and behavioral frequency predicting self-reported addiction could reflect reverse causation (e.g., people who feel addicted may develop moral disapproval of their behavior) or third-variable confounding. While the authors acknowledge this limitation, the hypotheses are framed in directional, quasi-causal language (moral incongruence 'predicting' feelings of addiction), which overstates what cross-sectional data can demonstrate.
issues.quote: This sample is cross-sectional, which limits the temporal ordering of variables.

issues.description: The study plans 8 moderation analyses but does not specify any correction for multiple comparisons in the primary hypothesis tests. While Holm-adjusted statistics are mentioned for bivariate correlations, no such adjustment is described for the primary moderation analyses. With 8 tests, the family-wise error rate is substantially inflated, increasing the risk of finding a significant interaction for pornography by chance or failing to find one for other behaviors.
issues.quote: In total, we will conduct 8 moderation analyses for moral disapproval and frequency, corresponding to the 8 target behaviors/variables of interest

issues.description: The NIDA-ASSIST has been substantially modified in several ways: adding a 'more than once per day' response option, including pornography and gambling as response options, broadening nicotine to include non-cigarette products, and adding cannabis separately. None of these modifications have been validated. The psychometric properties of the modified instrument are unknown, and the modifications may alter the measurement properties of the scale in unpredictable ways. The authors plan to average items with very different response scales (0-5 for frequency items and 0-6 for yes/no items), which is psychometrically questionable.
issues.quote: Responses to each of the above five items will be averaged for each substance of interest (i.e., alcohol, tobacco, non-tobacco nicotine, prescription drugs, illicit drugs, cannabis).

issues.description: The NIDA-ASSIST composite averages three frequency-based items scored 0-5 with two binary/ternary items scored 0, 3, or 6. Averaging these items without standardization or weighting means the two items with the 0-3-6 scale will disproportionately influence the composite score. This creates a composite with unclear psychometric properties and potentially distorted variance, which could affect the sensitivity of the outcome measure to detect interaction effects.
issues.quote: Participants will also respond to two questions... for each substance on 3 point scale (0 = No, Never; 3 = Yes, but not in the past 3 months; and 6 = Yes, In the past 3 months). Responses to each of the above five items will be averaged for each substance of interest

issues.description: In a general population sample, most substance use disorder symptom measures and problem gambling measures will have highly skewed distributions with floor effects (most people scoring zero or near-zero). This is especially true for less prevalent behaviors. Such distributions violate OLS regression assumptions and can severely attenuate interaction effects. While the authors mention checking assumptions and conducting supplemental analyses, they do not specify what alternative methods would be used, and the planned equivalence tests may not be robust to such violations.
issues.quote: Although Ordinary Least Squares techniques (such as the moderation analyses conducted by the Interactive application) in large sample sizes are often robust against some violations (Schmidt & Finan, 2018), in cases where assumptions are substantially violated, we will conduct supplemental analyses to test the robustness of our models, as appropriate.

issues.description: For each behavior, only participants who report engaging in the behavior will complete measures of problematic use. This creates different subsamples for each analysis with potentially different characteristics. Importantly, the selection into each subsample is non-random and related to the key predictor (behavioral frequency), which could introduce range restriction on the frequency variable and bias the estimated interaction effects differently across behaviors.
issues.quote: Only participants who endorse past-year use will complete further measures of problematic use.

issues.subcategory: Confound between moral disapproval and BPS item content
issues.description: Item 5 of the Brief Pornography Screen ('You continue to use pornography even though you feel guilty about it') directly taps into guilt/moral distress about pornography use. This creates construct overlap between the predictor (moral disapproval) and the outcome measure, which could artificially inflate the moral incongruence interaction for pornography relative to other behaviors where the outcome measures do not contain morally-laden items. This is a critical confound when the central hypothesis is that moral incongruence uniquely predicts pornography-related self-reported addiction.
issues.quote: 5. You continue to use pornography even though you feel guilty about it.

issues.description: The methods section states the PGSI uses a 4-point scale of 0 (never) to 3 (almost always), but the supplemental materials show the response options as Never (0), Sometimes (2), Most of the time (4), Almost Always (5). These are inconsistent—the supplemental version uses a non-standard scoring (0, 2, 4, 5) that differs from the validated PGSI scoring (0, 1, 2, 3). This discrepancy could affect the psychometric properties of the measure and comparability with prior research.
issues.quote: This 9-item measure requires participants to respond to a series of questions... on a 4-point scale of 0 (never) to 3 (almost always). Responses will be averaged.

issues.description: The methods section states the BPS uses a three-point scale of 0 (never) to 2 (very often) and that responses are summed. However, the supplemental materials show the scoring as Never (0), Occasionally (2), Very Often (4). This non-standard scoring (0, 2, 4 instead of 0, 1, 2) would produce different sum scores and potentially different psychometric properties than the validated version of the instrument.
issues.quote: by reporting the frequency they have experienced certain behaviors... on a three-point scale of 0 (never) to 2 (very often). Responses are summed.

issues.description: Religiousness is included as a covariate in all models, but it is also theoretically a key driver of moral disapproval (especially for pornography). Controlling for religiousness may partial out meaningful variance in moral disapproval that is central to the moral incongruence construct, potentially attenuating the interaction effect for pornography. Conversely, religiousness may be less related to moral disapproval of substances, creating differential suppression/attenuation across behaviors. This asymmetric confounding could bias the cross-behavior comparison that is central to the study's hypotheses.
issues.quote: In each case, we intend on including religiousness, age, and gender as covariates, as prior work has demonstrated clear links between such variables and self-reported problematic pornography use

issues.description: Gender is coded as binary (1 = male, 0 = not-male), which collapses all non-male gender identities into a single category. This is both a potential validity concern (non-binary, transgender, and female participants may differ substantially in their moral attitudes and addictive behaviors) and a representation concern. The 'not-male' coding is particularly problematic as it treats female participants and gender-diverse participants as equivalent.
issues.quote: gender (binary where 1 = male, and 0 =not-male)

issues.description: The gambling frequency measure combines highly heterogeneous activities (casino gambling, lottery tickets, fantasy sports, esports betting, sports betting, poker, online gambling) into a single frequency item. These activities differ substantially in their addictive potential, moral valence, and frequency patterns. A person who buys a weekly lottery ticket is treated equivalently to someone who gambles daily at a casino. This heterogeneity could attenuate the moral incongruence interaction for gambling if moral disapproval varies across gambling subtypes.
issues.quote: Examples of these types of activities include: gambling in casinos or online, buying lottery tickets, playing fantasy sports for money, placing bets on esports, placing bets on traditional sporting events, playing cards for money, placing bets online.

issues.description: The hypotheses create an asymmetric testing framework: for pornography, the authors test whether the interaction IS significant (standard NHST), while for other behaviors, they test whether the interaction is NOT significant (equivalence testing). This asymmetry means different standards of evidence are applied to different behaviors. Finding a significant interaction for pornography requires only p < .05, while concluding no interaction for other behaviors requires the confidence interval to fall entirely within the equivalence region. This creates a situation where the deck is stacked in favor of confirming the hypotheses.
issues.quote: We also expect to find that the interaction of moral disapproval of pornography use and pornography viewing frequency will positively predict self-reported levels of problematic or addictive pornography use... However, we do not expect to find that the interaction of moral disapproval of gambling and gambling frequency will significantly predict self-reported gambling disorder symptoms.

issues.description: The prevalence and social acceptability of the behaviors being compared vary enormously (from ~70% for alcohol to ~3.5% for prescription drug misuse). Behaviors with very high moral disapproval rates (e.g., illicit drugs) will have restricted variance on the moral disapproval measure, while behaviors with mixed moral views (e.g., pornography, gambling) will have greater variance. These base rate differences in both behavior frequency and moral disapproval could systematically affect the detectability of interaction effects across behaviors, independent of whether moral incongruence truly operates differently.
issues.quote: Given prevalence estimates associated with the various substances and behaviors of interest in our analyses (ranging from 3.5% of Americans who misuse prescription drugs within a given year to over 70% who consume alcohol

issues.subcategory: Inconsistent description of moral incongruence operationalization
issues.description: The introduction describes moral incongruence as 'the interaction of behavioral frequency and moral disapproval of a behavior,' but later in the methods, it is described as 'the interaction of moral disapproval of an action with severity of consequences from the action.' These are different operationalizations—one involves frequency and the other involves severity of consequences. This inconsistency creates confusion about what is actually being tested.
issues.quote: Central to the proposed study is the measurement of moral incongruence as the interaction of moral disapproval of an action with severity of consequences from the action.

issues.description: The frequency measures assess past 12-month behavior, the NIDA-ASSIST problematic use items assess past 3 months, and the Brief Pornography Screen assesses the past 6 months. These different time frames create temporal mismatches between predictors and outcomes that could differentially affect the analyses across behaviors. Someone could have used a substance frequently in the past year but not in the past 3 months, creating a disconnect between the frequency predictor and the problematic use outcome.
issues.quote: participants will report the frequency with which they have engaged in those behaviors over the past 12 months... In the past three months, how often have you had a strong desire or urge to use or engage in the following?

issues.description: The study relies entirely on self-report measures for both predictors and outcomes, creating shared method variance that could inflate associations. More critically, for the moral incongruence hypothesis, people who morally disapprove of a behavior they engage in may be more likely to endorse items about feeling 'out of control' or 'addicted' as a way of externalizing responsibility for behavior they view as wrong, rather than because they actually experience greater dysregulation. This response bias would be expected to operate across all behaviors, not just pornography, potentially undermining the uniqueness hypothesis.
issues.quote: the purpose of the present work is to test whether the moral incongruence model of problematic pornography use may generalize to addictions more broadly or whether it is unique to pornography use and sexual behavior.

issues.description: The study exclusively measures self-reported feelings of addiction and problematic use, without any objective or behavioral measures of actual dysregulation. This is particularly problematic because the central theoretical question is whether moral incongruence creates false perceptions of addiction versus reflecting actual dysregulation. Without objective measures, the study cannot distinguish between these possibilities for any of the behaviors studied.
issues.quote: This model posited that, for some people, self-reported feelings of addiction to pornography are less a representation of actual dysregulation and more a function of moral incongruence

issues.subcategory: Lack of formal comparison across behaviors
issues.description: The analytic plan tests each behavior separately but does not include a formal statistical comparison of interaction effect sizes across behaviors. Without directly comparing the magnitude of the moral incongruence interaction for pornography versus other behaviors (e.g., using confidence interval overlap tests or multi-group comparisons), the authors cannot rigorously conclude that the effect is 'unique' to pornography. Finding significance for one behavior and equivalence with null for another does not constitute a formal test of difference.
issues.quote: Interactions between moral disapproval and behavioral frequency will be tested for a variety of behaviors... to establish whether moral incongruence is related to self-reported feelings of addiction in various domains or if such links are unique to compulsive sexual behaviors.

issues.description: The methods section states pornography viewing frequency will be assessed on a scale from '1 (never) to 6 (more than once per day),' but the NIDA-ASSIST and supplemental materials show the scale as 0 (never) to 5 (more than once per day). This inconsistency in the starting value of the scale could affect centering and interaction term calculations.
issues.quote: Pornography viewing frequency will be assessed using the same modified frequency scale as is present on the ASSIST, wherein participants will report past-year frequency of pornography use on a scale of 1 (never) to 6 (more than once per day).

issues.subcategory: Ceiling effects on moral disapproval for illicit substances
issues.description: For illicit drug use and prescription drug misuse, moral disapproval is likely to be very high across the board (most people morally disapprove of illegal drug use), resulting in restricted variance on the moral disapproval measure. This ceiling effect would attenuate any interaction between moral disapproval and use frequency, making it harder to detect moral incongruence effects for these substances—not because the effect doesn't exist, but because of measurement limitations.
issues.quote: I believe that using illegal/illicit drugs is morally wrong.

issues.description: The authors state they do not anticipate needing to remove responses due to inattentive responding, relying entirely on YouGov's proprietary quality control. However, no specific attention check items are included in the survey, and the authors provide no details about what YouGov's quality control procedures entail. For a survey of this length covering sensitive topics, independent attention checks would strengthen data quality assurance.
issues.quote: As this data will be obtained via YouGov Opinion Polling, certain measures of quality control and responsiveness are guaranteed as a part of their data collection process based on their proprietary data collection standards. Accordingly, we do not anticipate having to remove responses from the dataset due to inattentive or invalid response styles

issues.description: No measure of social desirability is included. Given that the study asks about morally sensitive topics (pornography use, drug use, gambling) and moral attitudes simultaneously, social desirability could systematically bias responses. People high in social desirability may underreport both behavior frequency and overreport moral disapproval, which could artificially create or inflate the moral incongruence interaction. This bias may operate differently across behaviors (e.g., stronger for pornography and illicit drugs than for alcohol).
issues.quote: For each substance, we will ask participants to rate their agreement with the following statement 'I believe that using ________ is morally wrong'

issues.subcategory: Exploratory analysis contingency plan is vague
issues.description: The contingency plan for when hypotheses are not supported involves redefining the equivalence region using the lower bound of the 95% CI from the pornography interaction effect. However, this is a post-hoc adjustment that depends on the obtained results, which undermines the pre-registered nature of the analysis. The specific CI bounds are not known in advance, making this a data-dependent analytic decision rather than a truly pre-registered one.
issues.quote: In the event that, contrary to hypotheses, the effects of moral incongruence for gambling and substances exceed our region of equivalence based on our SESOI, we will conduct exploratory analyses wherein we redefine the region of equivalence using the lower bounds of the 95% CI for the standardized estimate for our pornography outcome.

issues.description: The methods state that 'Only participants who endorse past-year use will complete further measures of problematic use' but later state 'we will administer measures of problematic use and moral disapproval to all participants in the sample.' These statements directly contradict each other, creating ambiguity about who actually completes which measures.
issues.quote: Only participants who endorse past-year use will complete further measures of problematic use... we will administer measures of problematic use and moral disapproval to all participants in the sample.

issues.description: Moral disapproval—the key moderator variable in all analyses—is measured with a single item for each behavior. Single-item measures have unknown reliability, cannot be assessed for internal consistency, and are more susceptible to measurement error. Given that moral disapproval is the central construct in the study and its interaction with frequency is the primary test, the use of single-item measures introduces substantial measurement error that could attenuate interaction effects differentially across behaviors.
issues.quote: For each substance, we will ask participants to rate their agreement with the following statement 'I believe that using ________ is morally wrong' on a scale of 1 (strongly disagree) to 7 (strongly agree).

issues.subcategory: Pornography use measured only as solitary viewing
issues.description: The pornography frequency item in the supplemental materials specifies 'Viewed pornography alone (i.e., without a partner),' which excludes partnered pornography viewing. This restriction may not capture the full range of pornography use behaviors and could underestimate frequency for some participants, potentially affecting the interaction analyses.
issues.quote: Viewed pornography alone (i.e., without a partner)

issues.description: The paper uses multiple effect size metrics interchangeably (ΔR², f², Cohen's d, standardized β) when discussing prior findings and setting the SESOI. The conversions between these metrics are not always straightforward and depend on assumptions about the data. For example, the paper states 'ΔR2 = .014, f2 = .020, Cohen's d = .24' but the conversion from ΔR² to Cohen's d depends on sample size and model specification. This creates confusion about what exactly the SESOI represents and whether the equivalence bounds are appropriately calibrated.
issues.quote: Prior studies of moral incongruence have found moral incongruence to have small (ΔR2 = .014, f2 = .020, Cohen's d = .24, Grubbs, Kraus, et al., 2020; ΔR2 = .012, f2 = .016, Cohen's d = .22, Grubbs, Lee, et al., 2020), to moderate (ΔR2 = .072, f2 = .12, Cohen's d = .69; Grubbs, Kraus, et al., 2020), to relatively large (ΔR2 = .12, f2 = .23, Cohen's d = .97, Grubbs, Kraus, et al., 2020)

issues.subcategory: Conflation of stigma with moral disapproval
issues.description: The literature review cites evidence that individuals with substance use disorders 'morally disapprove of their own behaviors' and that gamblers view their behaviors as 'moral failure,' but these may reflect stigma and self-stigma rather than pre-existing moral disapproval. The temporal ordering matters: moral disapproval that develops after recognizing one's addiction (self-stigma) is conceptually different from pre-existing moral values that create incongruence. The study's cross-sectional design cannot distinguish between these, but the theoretical framework treats them as equivalent.
issues.quote: There is certainly evidence that many individuals with substance use disorders morally disapprove of their own behaviors (Matthews et al., 2017) and that individuals with gambling disorder often view their behaviors to be a moral failure (E. Miller & Thomas, 2017; Hing et al., 2016).
